claims.claim: In October Fireworks said attackers had reached only the secrets it stored for evaluation jobs.
claims.quote: environment variables, including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, were captured in certain affected accounts
claims.fix: October bulletin says environment variables used in evaluation jobs, including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, were captured in certain accounts, and that it had 'not detected evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data' based on its investigation at this time, with review of other potential access ongoing. 'Only' is the brief's gloss, not Fireworks' word.

claims.claim: Its update of 9 November says account and billing information was affected too, and for a limited set of accounts so were secrets, datasets and incomplete models.
claims.quote: For a limited set of accounts, we also discovered impact to secrets, datasets, and incomplete models.

claims.claim: a third-party cloud provider hosting its R&D machines was hit on 23 October and used to reach them on 24 October
claims.quote: A third-party cloud provider that hosted Fireworks R&D machines experienced a security incident on October 23.

claims.claim: Fireworks links the activity to a financially motivated group that sells stolen LLM access
claims.quote: a cybercriminal threat actor group, which is financially motivated and aimed at selling tokens
claims.fix: Source wording is 'selling tokens from unauthorized access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to illicit routing gateways' (LLMJacking); 'links' matches 'evidence indicates links'.

claims.claim: Fireworks says Inference, Training SDK and Nexus, which are zero data retention by default, show no impact.
claims.quote: We have not detected any impact to
claims.fix: Page lists Inference, Training SDK and Nexus as 'all zero data retention (ZDR) by default'.

claims.claim: Fixed in: not applicable (Fireworks lists hardening steps and has disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads for Batch Inference and dataset-based training)
claims.quote: we've disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads used by Batch Inference and dataset-based training

claims.claim: Severity: not stated in the bulletin
claims.quote: Searched whole update page for 'severity', 'CVE', 'high', 'Fixed': no severity rating; only 'close known critical vulnerabilities' under Further activity (a hardening step). October bulletin: no severity level, status 'Active monitoring'.

claims.claim: Stopgap: the October bulletin says to create new API keys for revoked ones, rotate third-party credentials, and review access logs
claims.quote: Replace revoked Fireworks API keys if you still need them.
claims.fix: Also 'Rotate third-party credentials identified in your notice' and work with issuing providers to review access logs.

claims.claim: If compromised: reply to your incident notification email
claims.quote: Reply to your incident notification email or contact
claims.fix: Update gives security-notice@fireworks.ai as alternative.

claims.claim: Anthropic says Fable and Mythos 5.2 are the same underlying model.
claims.quote: Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model.

claims.claim: Fable has stronger cyber and biology safeguards and is open to everyone; Mythos goes to vetted users through Anthropic's verification programs.
claims.quote: Claude Mythos 5.2 is available to vetted organizations that work in these dual-use areas.
claims.fix: Anthropic says 'Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards' and that Mythos is 'the same underlying model as Fable 5.2 without certain cybersecurity or biology safeguards'; Fable is 'available to all users'. Say 'has cyber and biology safeguards that Mythos lacks' rather than 'stronger'.

claims.claim: Fable costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output
claims.quote: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens

claims.claim: Artificial Analysis gives it 65 on its intelligence index, the highest so far.
claims.quote: scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
claims.fix: 65 is correct and the page ranks it #1 / 74 in the Intelligence section, but its own summary text says 'amongst the leading models in intelligence'. Prefer 'ranked first of 74 models listed'.

claims.claim: Anthropic's own numbers put it at 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2 against 62.3% for Opus 5.5
claims.quote: Fable 5.2 scored 69.9% and Opus 5.5 scored 62.3%

claims.claim: Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 as the daily driver for most coding and knowledge work
claims.quote: For most coding and knowledge tasks, we recommend that users start with Claude Opus 5.5, our strongest daily driver,
claims.fix: Source says 'most coding and knowledge tasks' and 'start with Claude Opus 5.5'; change 'work' to 'tasks'.

claims.claim: AWS says Fable 5.2 is a covered model, so by default its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review.
claims.quote: By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review.
claims.fix: Anthropic's own page says only 'For other customers, we have 30-day retention for safety monitoring' (eligible enterprises can use zero data retention); the 'covered model' and 'human review' wording is AWS's, as the brief attributes.

claims.fix: Title 'MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory'; authors David H. Yang, Blake Bullwinkel, Amanda Minnich, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Giorgio Severi (brief names no authors).
